requirements.quote:
Although TLS 1.3 does not use RSA key transport and so is not
directly susceptible to Bleichenbacher-type attacks [Blei98], if TLS
1.3 servers also support static RSA in the context of previous
versions of TLS, then it may be possible to impersonate the server
for TLS 1.3 connections [JSS15].
requirements.required_behavior: use a TLS 1.3 key-establishment mechanism other than RSA key transport
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use RSA key transport in TLS 1.3
requirements.why_checkable: TLS 1.3 cipher-suite and key-exchange dispatch can be inspected and tested for absence of static RSA key transport.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 implementations can prevent
this attack by disabling support for static RSA across all versions
of TLS.
requirements.condition: an implementation prevents the cross-version static-RSA impersonation attack described here
requirements.required_behavior: disable static RSA support in every supported TLS version
requirements.forbidden_behavior: leave static RSA enabled in an older TLS version sharing the TLS 1.3 server identity
requirements.why_checkable: Enabled cipher suites and key-exchange modes are concrete configuration that can be enumerated for every protocol version.

requirements.quote:
In principle, implementations might also be able to separate
certificates with different keyUsage bits for static RSA decryption
and RSA signature, but this technique relies on clients refusing to
accept signatures using keys in certificates that do not have the
digitalSignature bit set
requirements.condition: an implementation uses certificate separation as an alternative mitigation for static RSA and RSA signing
requirements.required_behavior: use separate certificates with distinct keyUsage authorization for static RSA decryption and RSA signatures
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse one certificate key without separating the decryption and signature keyUsage roles
requirements.why_checkable: Certificate configuration can be inspected for separate keys and the corresponding keyUsage bits.

requirements.quote:
this technique relies on clients refusing to
accept signatures using keys in certificates that do not have the
digitalSignature bit set
requirements.condition: a client validates an RSA signature whose certificate keyUsage extension lacks digitalSignature
requirements.why_checkable: A certificate-validation test can present a valid cryptographic signature under a certificate lacking the digitalSignature bit.
